The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against orders passed by SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SAT stands for the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
It serves as a legal body to hear appeals against rulings of financial regulators.
It has appellate jurisdiction over decisions made by SEBI.
Appeals against orders passed by IRDAI are brought before SAT.
Orders issued by PFRDA are also appealable at the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
Exam questions frequently ask which regulatory bodies fall under SAT's jurisdiction: SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA.
Note that SAT is not restricted to SEBI alone; insurance (IRDAI) and pension (PFRDA) appeals are also heard here.
